Order 
This criminal appeal under Section 14A (2) of the Scheduled Castes & Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 has been preferred challenging the order dated 24.01.2026 in BA No.55/2026 by the Special Judge, SC/ST (PA) Act 1989, Neemuch (MP) whereby the application for anticipatory bail in connection with FIR/Crime No.01/2026 registered at Police Station-AJK,
District- Neemuch (MP) for offence punishable under Sections 376(2)(n) and 506 of the IPC and sections 3(1)(w)(ii) and 3(2)(v) of the Scheduled Caste & Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities)
Act, 1989 has been rejected.

sentences.text: Facts of the case in brief are that, a crime No.01/2026 was registered at P.S.- AJK, District- Neemuch on a written complaint dated 07.01.2026 by the prosecutrix belonging to scheduled caste community against appellant/accused who does not belongs to SC or ST community regarding the duration of offence committed from 02.01.2012 till 30.04.2024 when the appellant/accused was posted as Assistant Sub-Inspector at P.S.-Manasa, District- Neemuch (MP).

It was NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:6011 2 CRA-1233-2026 alleged that during the posting of appellant/accused as Assistant Sub-Inspector at P.S.-Manasa appellant reached her village and asked cell number of the victim on the pretext that if he requires any information he will call her.
Thereafter, appellant/accused intimated the victim that he has some dispute with her wife and proposed her for marriage.
When she repeatedly asked appellant/accused for marriage then he always sought time and continuously exploited her sexually.

In the year 2024 appellant threatened her to kill saying that you belongs to the schedule caste community therefore he cannot marry her and wherever she goes to work appellant/ accused extended the threat to her.
Earlier also she filed applications but no applications was taken into consideration.

1 application of the appellant recording the finding that bar under section 18 of the of the Scheduled Caste & Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is attracted in this case.

Challenging the impugned order this criminal appeal has been preferred on the ground that in the year 2019 prosecutrix made complaint against the appellant which was withdrawn by her and thereafter in the year 2022 prosecutrix again made the complaint which was subsequently withdrawn by her and so no offence as alleged by prosecutrix is made out against the present appellant.

sentences.text: In light of the parameters in relation to the applicability of Section 18 of the Act emanating from afore-discussed various decisions of this Court, the proposition could be summarised that as the provision of Section 18 of the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribes, Act, 1989 with express language excludes the applicability of Section 438, Cr.PC, it creates a bar against grant of anticipatory bail in absolute terms in relations to the arrest of a person who faces specific accusations of having committed the offence under the Scheduled Caste and Scheduled Tribe Act.

sentences.text: The benefit of anticipatory bail for such an accused is taken off.
6.1 The absolute nature of bar, however, could be read and has to be applied with a rider.

In a given case where on the face of it the offence under Section 3 of the Act is found to have not been made out and that the accusations relating to the commission of such offence are devoid of prima facie merits, the Court has a room to exercise the discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the accused under Section 438 of the Code.

6.2 Non-making of prima facie case about the commission of offence is perceived to be such a situation where the Court can arrive at such a conclusion in the first blush itself or by way of the first impression upon very reading of the averments in the FIR.
The contents and the allegations in the FIR would be decisive in this regard.

Furthermore, in reaching a conclusion as to whether a prima facie offence is made out or not, it would not be permissible for the Court to NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:6011 4 CRA-1233-2026 travel into the evidentiary realm or to consider other materials, nor the Court could advert to conduct a mini trial."

7. The contents of the First Information Report of crime No.1/2026 registered at P.S.-AJK Neemuch reveals that appellant Mahesh Shukla was posted as Assistant Sub-Inspector of Police in P.S.-Manasa in the year 2012 and during the official visits he came in contact with the victim who belongs to Banchada community which falls under the scheduled caste category and resident of a village within the jurisdiction of P.S. - Manasa.

Appellant asked the cell number of the victim and developed close acquaintance with the victim and thereafter, established physical relations persuading the victim that he will marry her and continued that relationship knowing the caste identity of the victim/ prosecutrix.
Appellant got retired in the year 2022 and continued to exploit the victim physically and extended the threat that if she will marry any other person then he will kill the victim.

8. The above contents of the First Information Report reveals that appellant was a public servant being Assistant Sub-Inspector in the M.P. Police posted at police station where the victim belonging to scheduled caste was residing.
Appellant was already married with living spouse and continued the relationship with the victim abusing his position.
In the Indian Penal Code, 1860 "Sex by abuse of authority" has been recognized in dual ways.
One under the sub-clause of Section 376 (2) if proved as non consensual and under section 376 C if proved as consensual.
If proved to be consensual sexual intercourse obtained by a public servant it would fall under Section 376 C of the IPC.
The same offence has been recognized under section 68 of the BNS, 2023.

The offence under section 376 C of the IPC is punishable upto 10 years RI.
8.
There is material that appellant was acquainted with the caste identity of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:6011 5 CRA-1233-2026 the victim.

Accordingly, provisions of section 3(2)(v)
of the Scheduled Caste & Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 are attracted in this case and it cannot be concluded that accusations relating the commission of above offence are devoid of merits.

sentences.text:
Accordingly, there is no room to exercise the discretion to grant anticipatory bail to the accused under section 438 of the Cr.P.C., 1973 on the reference of Aparna Joseph@Current KunjuKunju (Supra), Vijayan (Supra), Dr. Subhash Kashinath Mahajan (Supra), State of M.P.
(Supra) and Manju Devi (Supra).

Accordingly the trial court has rightly concluded that bar of section 18 of the Scheduled Caste & Scheduled Tribe (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 is attracted in this case and there is no scope for grant of anticipatory bail to the appellant.
